themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 32 this week compared to a 9.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 256% increase (z-score: 4.49)—suggesting rapid pavement or pothole issues emerging across CD316 this week.
evidence: 32 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score: 4.49)
Concurrently, root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints up 540% last week (4 vs. 0.6 avg, z-score: 4.85), suggesting subsurface infrastructure issues may be surfacing
414 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (270 alterations), indicating active construction that may be damaging streets or exacerbating existing conditions
reporting_angles: Map where the 32 complaints are concentrated this week—are they clustered near active construction sites or specific corridors?
Interview DSNY and DOT about whether spring thaw, heavy rain, or construction activity is driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 3 this week versus 0.6 weekly average—a 380% spike (z-score: 4.91)—indicating newly missing or damaged signage across the district this week.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (380% increase, z-score: 4.91)
Timing aligns with broader street infrastructure spike, suggesting possible vandalism, weather damage, or construction-related removal
Low absolute volume but extremely sharp statistical deviation indicates new phenomenon rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: Ground-truth: walk high-complaint areas to identify patterns (residential vs. commercial, specific neighborhoods)
Contact DOT about whether signs are being removed for construction or if vandalism/weather is the driver

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed garbage collection complaints surged to 13 last week versus a 1.5 weekly average—a 767% spike (z-score: 6.93)—indicating acute collection failures across CD316 over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 13 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (767% spike, z-score: 6.93, severity: high)
Coincides with broader unsanitary condition complaints (555 over 90 days), suggesting collection failures are creating visible neighborhood decay
One of the highest z-scores in the dataset, indicating this is statistically anomalous and recent
reporting_angles: Interview residents in blocks with multiple missed pickups—how long have collections been failing and what's the impact (odor, rats, blocked sidewalks)?
Contact DSNY Sanitation to determine if staffing shortages, equipment breakdowns, or route changes caused the spike last week

themes_detail.label: Uncontrolled Tree Growth & Overgrowth
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 4 two weeks ago versus 0.4 weekly average—a 967% spike (z-score: 7.49, the highest in dataset)—indicating widespread vegetation overgrowth across CD316.
evidence: 4 overgrown tree/branch complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 7.49—highest z-score in dataset)
Timing suggests spring growth cycle or delayed maintenance from prior season
May pose safety hazards (visibility, overhead damage) and quality-of-life issues if branches block sidewalks or overhanging property
reporting_angles: Document specific locations with hazardous overgrowth—do branches obstruct sight lines, create pedestrian hazards, or damage storefronts?
Contact Parks Dept about tree maintenance schedules and whether budget/staffing limits are preventing proactive trimming

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 7 last week versus 1.4 weekly average—a 409% increase (z-score: 4.62)—suggesting rapid expansion or public concern about unlicensed or nuisance cannabis shops in CD316.
evidence: 7 cannabis retailer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% spike, z-score: 4.62)
Timing aligns with state/city expansion of legal cannabis retail licensing—possible influx of new storefronts
Complaints likely reflect resident concerns about storefront locations, odor, loitering, or unlicensed operations
reporting_angles: Are complaints coming from specific neighborhoods or near schools/youth centers? Map the locations of new cannabis shops vs. complaints.
Interview SBS and NYPD about cannabis retail licensing enforcement—are unlicensed shops operating? How many licensed retailers opened in CD316 recently?
